subject: Channel-strip send slots in the Mixer: the Accessibility shape of an assigned send beside an empty one
question: Which element is an ASSIGNED send slot, and how does it differ from an empty one in role, description, help, title and value?

reverify.command: python3 Scripts/livekit/live_291_endpoints_and_send_slots_in_every_locale.py --locale ko (with LPM_EVIDENCE_ROOT exported, Logic in Korean on lpm-locale-campaign with the Mixer shown; --locale en after switching to English)
reverify.expected: send_slot_count_matches_witness, occupancy_matches_knob_witness and send_assignment_then_undo pass: in the send-after reading the target strip's witnessed sends are [button, unoccupied] then [group, occupied, described by the chosen bus], the product reads observed_empty then occupied_unknown_destination with level_raw 0, no knob belongs to no slot, and the Mixer has one more strip whose input reads the bus; the after-undo reading equals the before reading. The manual dump that first took this reading: On lpm-locale-campaign with the Mixer showing: `swift Scripts/livekit/ax_mixer_strip_dump.swift --strip 1 --probe-index`; select a bus in strip 1's send slot with `Scripts/livekit/ax_routing_slot_menu_probe.swift --slot-prefix <that slot's help> --slot-index <its probe-index> --mute-labels none --select <bus title>`; dump strip 1 and strip 2 again; then undo with Edit menu item 1 and dump strip 1 once more.
reverify.cost: Logic running with the fixture and the Mixer shown; one send assignment and one undo per language; ~3 min, plus a relaunch per language switch

method: Logic 12.3 on lpm-locale-campaign, first in Korean, then quit and relaunched in English, then back in Korean. With the Mixer showing, Scripts/livekit/ax_mixer_strip_dump.swift dumped strip 1 (Audio 1) and strip 2 pre-order, every element to 20 levels, with AXRole, AXRoleDescription, AXDescription, AXHelp, AXTitle, AXValue, AXValueDescription, AXPosition and AXSize. A send was then assigned on strip 1 by ax_routing_slot_menu_probe.swift: AXPress on the send slot, AXPress on the menu item titled `버스 256` (`Bus 256` in English) — the bus #291's first live run had chosen. The probe's Mute control was disabled for these runs (`--mute-labels` given a label no element carries), so no Mute was pressed. The assignment was confirmed by Logic's own Edit menu item 1, not by the slot. Strips 1 and 2 and the new strip were dumped, then Edit menu item 1 undid the send and strip 1 was dumped again. The raw dumps are in the evidence file; the rows below are copied from it verbatim.

conclusion:
An assigned send is not a send-slot button. In both languages it is an AXGroup with no help, described by the DESTINATION (`버스 256` in Korean, `B256` in English), holding a bypass checkbox and a list button, and its next sibling is the AXSlider whose help begins with the send-level-knob title. The button that precedes the group in the walk is a NEW empty slot: it sits below the group on screen, and the strip's children run bottom to top. The same assignment gave every other strip a second empty `send button` and the Mixer one more strip, an Aux whose input reads the bus; the undo removed both. What distinguishes the two slot shapes is therefore the ROLE (AXButton vs AXGroup), the HELP (the send-slot title vs none) and the DESCRIPTION (`send button` vs the destination), and it is the same in both languages except for the words: role is not localised, the help and the knob's description are, and the destination is abbreviated in English only.

This contradicts the 2026-09-13 record on its own stated limit: it identified the assigned slot as the `send button` immediately preceding the knob, which these dumps show to be the empty slot, so its reading of that slot's menu mark was taken on an empty slot. A reader that looks for the knob right after a send button finds none, and one that counts send buttons counts the empty ones only.
limits: One strip (an audio track with no inserts), one send, one destination bus, one project, two languages. A strip with two assigned sends was not dumped, so the order of two groups and their knobs is inferred from the bottom-to-top order seen here, not measured.

The destination named in the group's description was read for one bus. A renamed bus, a send to an existing Aux, and the eight other languages were not read, so the description is not established as a stable destination identifier.

The group's list button and its menu were not opened, so whether that menu marks the destination is unmeasured; the 2026-09-13 mark reading is undermined for the slot it was taken on and not replaced.
The destination bus had no receiving strip, so Logic created one (`Aux 4`). Whether a send to a bus some strip already receives also adds the empty send row was not measured.
`pos` and `size` were added to the dump tool after the first Korean dump of strip 1 was taken; that dump carries none.
